items.title: Efficient Reasoning Training Does Not Always Harm CoT Faithfulness and Monitorability
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether efficient Chain-of-Thought (CoT) training harms faithfulness and monitorability in large language models. The authors fine-tune models using three distinct length-pressure methods and evaluate their impact on how well the CoT reflects the model's decision-making process. Their contribution lies in demonstrating that efficient reasoning training does not *always* negatively affect CoT faithfulness, depending on the specific efficiency method and task.
items.figure_caption: Efficient reasoning training reduces CoT faithfulness but largely preserves monitorability. (1) We train models with three methods that reward CoT length differently. (2) Then we measure whether the CoT predicts the model’s answers on related inputs (faithfulness) and whether it reveals when an intervention influenced the answer (monitorability). (3) In this example, a ∼ \( \sim \) 70% shorter CoT loses faithfulness due to output inconsistency, while monitorability is unchanged.

items.title: FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution
items.abstract: FrugalEvo introduces a cost-aware evolutionary framework for LLM-guided program optimization. It leverages a two-tiered LLM approach, with a powerful LLM guiding strategy and a cheaper LLM implementing and refining code, to maximize performance gain per unit cost. The contribution lies in this cost-efficient design and a new metric, BA-AUC, for evaluating performance within a fixed budget.

items.title: HazardWeaver: Scientific Route Selection for Hazard Analysis Agents
items.abstract: HazardWeaver addresses the challenge of AI agents selecting appropriate scientific methods for hazard analysis by formulating it as state-dependent route selection. Its core method involves compiling evidence-linked conditions for scientific applicability and representing executable capabilities in a graph to check compatibility. This enables agents to dynamically choose and adapt scientific workflows based on evolving evidence and available tools.

items.title: HyperBrowseComp: A Multilingual and Multimodal Stress Test for Web-Browsing Agents
items.abstract: HyperBrowseComp is a new benchmark designed to rigorously test web-browsing agents. Its core method involves creating extremely challenging, multilingual, and multimodal questions that require agents to locate obscure information, follow complex clue chains, and synthesize data from diverse sources like videos and scanned documents. The contribution is a robust evaluation tool that pushes the boundaries of agent capabilities in persistent information seeking, going beyond simple parametric knowledge.
items.figure_caption: Example question and evidence route from HyperBrowseComp . Solving it requires locating a specific moment in a video, grounding the scene to a real-world location, and retrieving information from a financial report.

items.title: MobiAgent: Dual-Loop Recursive Policy Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation
items.abstract: MobiAgent tackles long-horizon mobile manipulation by introducing a dual-loop framework for robust deployment and continuous self-improvement. The Inner Loop uses a Vision-Language Model to dynamically compose atomic skills for receding-horizon planning and error recovery. The Outer Loop recursively refines these skills through self-generated trajectories, enabling continuous learning and adaptation beyond initial training.
items.figure_caption: Overview of MobiAgent. MobiAgent solves a long-horizon picking_up_trash task by interleaving dynamic planning, skill-conditioned execution, and critic-guided recovery. The rollout trace illustrates a failed placement where the can drops outside the trash. In response, MobiAgent triggers replanning, guiding the robot to approach the displaced can, re-grasp it, and complete the task. This behavior is driven by our dual-loop framework (bottom left), which couples an online Inner Loop executing atomic skills with an offline Outer Loop that autonomously curates data for continuous policy evolution. The bottom right shows real-robot deployment on paper, bottle, and can disposal, as well as pouring blue particles into a cup.

items.title: NeutronGym: Physics-Graded Neutron Instrument Design for LLM Agents
items.abstract: NeutronGym is a novel, executable environment designed to test whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can truly perform physics-based design rather than just recall information. It allows LLM agents to build neutron instruments by validating tools, with McStas ray-tracing and a physics-graded ladder evaluating their creations. The paper's core contribution is this physics-graded environment, which demonstrates current LLMs struggle with complex scientific instrument design, even after training.

items.title: IDRF: Inverse-Distilled Reward Fine-tuning of Masked Discrete Diffusion Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces IDRF, a framework for efficiently fine-tuning masked discrete diffusion models with rewards. IDRF replaces computationally expensive sequence-level KL divergence with an "inverse-distillation regularization" that is provably equivalent under optimal conditions. This allows for reward optimization using the model's own few-step sampler, achieving strong performance across various generation tasks without needing a separate reference model.
items.figure_caption: IDRF (ours) across DNA, images, and text. Reward-only fine-tuning and IDRF sample with the same budget of 8 8 , 4 4 , and 32 32 steps. Reward-only fine-tuning hacks the reward: DNA lacks accessibility (ATAC-Acc), images blur, and reviews degenerate into repetition that rarely ends with EOS. IDRF avoids these failures.

items.title: UniIntervene++: An Adaptive Intervention Agent for Efficient Real-World Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: UniIntervene++ introduces an adaptive intervention agent for online reinforcement learning in robots. It learns to dynamically switch between autonomous execution and various assisted behaviors by formulating them as "Options" within a unified semi-Markov decision process. This approach ensures interventions remain relevant as the robot's competence evolves, leading to more efficient real-world learning.

items.title: CLIMB: Confidence-Guided Complementary Evidence for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.abstract: CLIMB is a training-free framework for multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that improves knowledge-intensive visual question answering. It first creates a diverse pool of relevant textual evidence using a redundancy-reducing objective. Then, it refines the answer by selecting evidence based on relevance, specificity, and cross-modal alignment, only accepting an updated answer if it demonstrably increases confidence.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of multimodal RAG approaches. (a) Standard methods Cocchi et al. (2025) ; Caffagni et al. (2024b) ; Yan and Xie (2024) rely on Top-K similarity selection, which often produces redundant evidence with limited coverage and lacks explicit quality control for answer generation. (b) Our CLIMB framework addresses these limitations through two key innovations: diversity-aware evidence construction that balances relevance and complementarity to build a non-redundant passage pool, and confidence-controlled decoding that uses multi-faceted scoring and monotonic confidence constraints to ensure reliable answer updates.

items.title: Passing the Test You Trained On: Re-evaluating Prompt-Injection Detectors for LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper re-evaluates prompt-injection detectors used by LLM agents, finding that their performance on public benchmarks doesn't reliably predict their effectiveness within actual agents. By replaying tool calls from agent benchmarks, the authors demonstrate significant performance discrepancies and poor transferability of detection rankings across different benchmarks. Their contribution highlights the inadequacy of current evaluation methods and suggests that the training data's characteristics heavily influence detector performance.

items.title: 4DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agents on Inverse Graphics of Dynamic Scenes
items.abstract: 4DCodeBench is a new benchmark for evaluating AI agents' ability to perform 4D inverse graphics by generating executable code that reconstructs dynamic scenes from videos. The core method involves agents translating visual observations into compact representations of scene structure and dynamics, often requiring them to implement physical simulations. The contribution lies in providing a diverse set of real-world and synthetic videos to test this capability, revealing that current models struggle with complex dynamics despite strong static reconstruction skills.

items.title: Credit Where It Matters: Dependency-Aware Policy Optimization for Terminal Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces Dependency-Aware Group Policy Optimization (DepGPO) for reinforcement learning agents operating in terminal environments. DepGPO addresses the issue of irrelevant credit assignment by constructing a command dependency graph from execution traces. It then traces backward from task verification results to assign credit specifically to commands that directly influenced the outcome, thereby improving learning efficiency.

items.title: CVE2AP: Automated Generation of PDDL-Encoded Attack Paths via Large Language Models
items.abstract: CVE2AP automates the creation of formal attack path models in PDDL from natural language CVE descriptions. It leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) with structured prompting and an error-feedback loop to overcome the limitations of manual expert-driven modeling, enabling scalable and dynamic cybersecurity analysis.

items.title: Do Large Language Models Know Colombian Law? A Reliability Benchmark for the Colombian Legal System
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel, expert-validated benchmark to assess the reliability of Large Language Models (LLMs) on Colombian law. The benchmark, comprising 1,042 questions across ten legal areas and three formats, reveals significant limitations: while LLMs can be relevant, their factual accuracy on free-text legal answers is consistently low (below 0.45), highlighting a critical gap in their current capabilities for legal applications outside the US.

items.title: Jumping the Line: Exploiting Length Predictions in LLM Scheduling
items.abstract: This paper introduces JIL, an attack that exploits length predictions in LLM schedulers. JIL adds an adversarial suffix to requests, causing schedulers to underestimate their length and thus grant them higher priority. This manipulation leads to significantly faster completion times for adversarial requests.

items.title: Measure Less, Know More: Self-Supervised Test-Time Feature Acquisition
items.abstract: This paper proposes ECHO-$k$, a self-supervised method for efficiently acquiring relevant features from multimodal data at test time. It leverages a foundation model's internal representations as proxy targets to learn a task-agnostic policy for selecting the most informative modalities, thereby reducing acquisition costs while improving downstream performance.

items.title: Threat-Preserving Representation Sensitivity in Agent-Security Benchmarks
items.abstract: This paper introduces Threat-Preserving Representation Sensitivity (TPRS) to evaluate how benchmark representations affect LLM agent security evaluations. TPRS measures changes in attack success rate (ASR) when only the agent-visible representation is altered, keeping other factors constant. The study demonstrates that modifying tool names within benchmarks significantly impacts ASR, highlighting a crucial flaw in current security evaluation methods.

items.title: When a Correct Reward Is Not Enough: Diagnosing and Guiding PPO in an Analytically Solved Broker-Trader Game
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) can effectively learn optimal strategies in a financial game with an analytical solution. The core method involves training a PPO agent to act as a broker in a broker-trader game, using a derived reward function. The contribution lies in demonstrating that while PPO can approach the optimal solution in simpler scenarios, it struggles to achieve accuracy in the presence of stochastic market noise, even when supervised learning confirms the actor's capacity.

items.title: Divergence controls entropy in distillation
items.abstract: This paper reveals that the choice of divergence function in distillation directly controls the student model's entropy. Specifically, forward KL divergence inflates student entropy, while reverse KL deflates it. This finding offers a new entropic perspective on distillation, explaining observed behaviors and highlighting divergence as an implicit entropy regularizer.

items.title: FALCON: A Model and Dataset Agnostic Framework for Synthetic Data Generation for NL2SQL Pairs
items.abstract: FALCON is a framework that generates realistic and ambiguity-aware synthetic NL-to-SQL data. It addresses the limitations of existing methods by producing complex queries that better reflect real-world challenges, using reserved-word SQL seeding and persona-based prompting. The framework's contribution lies in its ability to create high-quality, difficulty-preserving data cost-effectively, improving the robustness of NL2SQL models.
items.figure_caption: Simplified architecture of the FALCON pipeline. It integrates systematic seeding, SQL and NL generation with CoT, and a multistage filtering process (Ambiguity, Reward, and Prompt-based), to produce high-quality NL-to-SQL pairs. items.summary: Formula 1 drivers expressed frustration and a sense of powerlessness due to a software glitch during the Bahrain Grand Prix that impacted their car's performance.

items.description: The design language that makes your AI harness better at design.

items.summary: This repository provides a comprehensive guide to marketing skills, including CRO, copywriting, SEO, analytics, and growth engineering, specifically tailored for Claude Code and AI agents.

items.description: Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
items.summary: This repository's core function is to make AI agents adopt the persona of a lazy senior developer, prioritizing minimal effort and code reuse to achieve the "best code" by avoiding writing new code.
This repository enables agents to generate CAD models from natural language descriptions, effectively giving them "CAD superpowers" by translating text into design.

items.description: Give your AI agent eyes to see the entire internet. Read & search Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili, XiaoHongShu — one CLI, zero API fees.
items.summary: Agent-Reach provides a unified CLI to grant AI agents internet vision, enabling them to read and search platforms like Twitter, Reddit, and YouTube without API fees.

items.description: Developer-first error tracking and performance monitoring
items.summary: Sentry is a developer-first platform that provides robust error tracking and performance monitoring to help teams identify, debug, and resolve issues in their applications.

items.description: World's first open-source, agentic video production system. 12 production pipelines, 100+ tools, 700+ agent skill and production-knowledge files. Turn your AI coding assistant into a full video production studio.
items.summary: OpenMontage is the first open-source, agentic video production system, offering 12 pipelines and over 700 skills to transform AI coding assistants into comprehensive video studios.

papers.abstract: This paper re-evaluates prompt-injection detectors used by LLM agents, finding that their performance on public benchmarks doesn't reliably predict their effectiveness within actual agents. By replaying tool calls from agent benchmarks, the authors demonstrate significant performance discrepancies and poor transferability of detection rankings across different benchmarks. Their contribution highlights the inadequacy of current evaluation methods and suggests that the training data's characteristics heavily influence detector performance.

papers.title: 4DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agents on Inverse Graphics of Dynamic Scenes
papers.abstract: 4DCodeBench is a new benchmark for evaluating AI agents' ability to perform 4D inverse graphics by generating executable code that reconstructs dynamic scenes from videos. The core method involves agents translating visual observations into compact representations of scene structure and dynamics, often requiring them to implement physical simulations. The contribution lies in providing a diverse set of real-world and synthetic videos to test this capability, revealing that current models struggle with complex dynamics despite strong static reconstruction skills.

papers.title: Credit Where It Matters: Dependency-Aware Policy Optimization for Terminal Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Dependency-Aware Group Policy Optimization (DepGPO) for reinforcement learning agents operating in terminal environments. DepGPO addresses the issue of irrelevant credit assignment by constructing a command dependency graph from execution traces. It then traces backward from task verification results to assign credit specifically to commands that directly influenced the outcome, thereby improving learning efficiency.

papers.title: CVE2AP: Automated Generation of PDDL-Encoded Attack Paths via Large Language Models
papers.abstract: CVE2AP automates the creation of formal attack path models in PDDL from natural language CVE descriptions. It leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) with structured prompting and an error-feedback loop to overcome the limitations of manual expert-driven modeling, enabling scalable and dynamic cybersecurity analysis.

papers.title: Do Large Language Models Know Colombian Law? A Reliability Benchmark for the Colombian Legal System
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel, expert-validated benchmark to assess the reliability of Large Language Models (LLMs) on Colombian law. The benchmark, comprising 1,042 questions across ten legal areas and three formats, reveals significant limitations: while LLMs can be relevant, their factual accuracy on free-text legal answers is consistently low (below 0.45), highlighting a critical gap in their current capabilities for legal applications outside the US.

papers.title: Jumping the Line: Exploiting Length Predictions in LLM Scheduling
papers.abstract: This paper introduces JIL, an attack that exploits length predictions in LLM schedulers. JIL adds an adversarial suffix to requests, causing schedulers to underestimate their length and thus grant them higher priority. This manipulation leads to significantly faster completion times for adversarial requests.

papers.title: Measure Less, Know More: Self-Supervised Test-Time Feature Acquisition
papers.abstract: This paper proposes ECHO-$k$, a self-supervised method for efficiently acquiring relevant features from multimodal data at test time. It leverages a foundation model's internal representations as proxy targets to learn a task-agnostic policy for selecting the most informative modalities, thereby reducing acquisition costs while improving downstream performance.

papers.title: Threat-Preserving Representation Sensitivity in Agent-Security Benchmarks
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Threat-Preserving Representation Sensitivity (TPRS) to evaluate how benchmark representations affect LLM agent security evaluations. TPRS measures changes in attack success rate (ASR) when only the agent-visible representation is altered, keeping other factors constant. The study demonstrates that modifying tool names within benchmarks significantly impacts ASR, highlighting a crucial flaw in current security evaluation methods.

papers.title: When a Correct Reward Is Not Enough: Diagnosing and Guiding PPO in an Analytically Solved Broker-Trader Game
papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) can effectively learn optimal strategies in a financial game with an analytical solution. The core method involves training a PPO agent to act as a broker in a broker-trader game, using a derived reward function. The contribution lies in demonstrating that while PPO can approach the optimal solution in simpler scenarios, it struggles to achieve accuracy in the presence of stochastic market noise, even when supervised learning confirms the actor's capacity.

papers.title: Divergence controls entropy in distillation
papers.abstract: This paper reveals that the choice of divergence function in distillation directly controls the student model's entropy. Specifically, forward KL divergence inflates student entropy, while reverse KL deflates it. This finding offers a new entropic perspective on distillation, explaining observed behaviors and highlighting divergence as an implicit entropy regularizer.

papers.title: FALCON: A Model and Dataset Agnostic Framework for Synthetic Data Generation for NL2SQL Pairs
papers.abstract: FALCON is a framework that generates realistic and ambiguity-aware synthetic NL-to-SQL data. It addresses the limitations of existing methods by producing complex queries that better reflect real-world challenges, using reserved-word SQL seeding and persona-based prompting. The framework's contribution lies in its ability to create high-quality, difficulty-preserving data cost-effectively, improving the robustness of NL2SQL models.
papers.figure_caption: Simplified architecture of the FALCON pipeline. It integrates systematic seeding, SQL and NL generation with CoT, and a multistage filtering process (Ambiguity, Reward, and Prompt-based), to produce high-quality NL-to-SQL pairs.
